Radiology Report
Date: 09/19/2026
Patient: Ja Hand, 69-year-old female

Examination: MRI thoracolumbar spine

Findings:
MRI thoracolumbar spine 09/19/2026: acute osteoporotic L3 compression fracture with bone marrow edema on STIR imaging.

Impression:
There is an acute osteoporotic compression fracture at the L3 vertebral body, demonstrated by bone marrow edema on STIR sequences. No other acute abnormalities are identified.

Recommendations:
Clinical correlation is advised. Follow-up imaging may be considered based on clinical scenario.

Spine Intervention Consultation
Date: 09/25/2026
Patient: Ja Hand, 69-year-old female

History:
Back pain began 08/29/2026 after lifting a laundry basket, 4 weeks before this visit. Pain NRS 8/10 despite 3 weeks of optimal non-surgical management with acetaminophen and calcitonin nasal spray, a thoracolumbar brace and activity modification. Pain has worsened over the past two weeks despite bracing.

Clinical Findings:
Seen in the outpatient spine clinic; not hospitalized for this fracture.

Plan:
Referred for DEXA bone density testing and osteoporosis education; enrolled in the osteoporosis treatment program. Continue current pain management and bracing. Follow-up to assess response to treatment and consider further intervention if pain persists or worsens.
